title: Implement negotiated PipeWire capture stream
description:
Create the PipeWire capture stream wrapper that connects to a PipeWire source, negotiates format/rate/channels, and copies audio into a caller-supplied ring buffer from the realtime process callback.

Before editing, inspect:
- src/audio/AudioRingBuffer.hpp for the ring buffer write() interface this stream will target.
- src/pipewire/PipeWireContext.hpp for the pw_thread_loop and pw_core objects established in Phase B; this stream must use the Phase-B-owned thread loop rather than creating a new one.
- Any existing PipeWire or audio headers under src/ for conventions.
- The PipeWire 0.3 spa_pod and pw_stream APIs for format negotiation patterns.

Do not infer APIs, schemas, behavior, or file contents; inspect the referenced files first.

Implement PipeWireCaptureStream with:
- Construction accepting a target node ID (or default source), desired sample format, sample rate, and channel count.
- Format negotiation: build an SPA pod with the requested params, register the stream, and read back the negotiated format from the param_changed callback. Expose the negotiated format, sample rate, and channel count so callers know exactly what was agreed.
- A realtime process callback (on_process) that copies frames from the PipeWire buffer into the ring buffer. The callback must not allocate, lock, do file I/O, touch Qt, or call into compression libraries.
- Stream lifecycle: start(), stop(), and destroy/cleanup methods. Handle the PipeWire thread loop correctly (lock/unlock around state changes, not inside the process callback).
- Expose whether the negotiated format matches the requested format (native capture) versus requiring quantization or resampling, so downstream can report capture fidelity honestly.
- Emit lightweight status changes (connected, disconnected, error, format-renegotiated) via an enum or callback, not via Qt signals.

Do not perform any file writing, compression, or GUI work in this unit.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Visualization contract: PipeWireCaptureStream owns a bounded, preallocated CaptureVisualizationSnapshot publisher. The realtime callback may decimate/copy frames into a fixed-size double buffer and publish a sequence number, but must not allocate or notify Qt. The snapshot contains a bounded sample window with corresponding peak/RMS data; it is separate from, and must never drain or retain references into, AudioRingBuffer.
acceptance_criteria: src/audio/PipeWireCaptureStream.hpp exists and declares the capture stream class with start(), stop(), and negotiated-format accessors
src/audio/PipeWireCaptureStream.cpp exists and compiles cleanly against PipeWire 0.3 headers
The process callback (on_process or equivalent) contains no std::mutex, no malloc/new, no file I/O, no Qt includes, and no compression calls
Negotiated format, sample rate, and channel count are exposed via public accessors
A method or accessor reports whether the capture is native or converted (quantized/resampled)
Stream lifecycle methods (start, stop, cleanup) lock the PipeWire thread loop outside the process callback
No #include of Qt, libsndfile, or FLAC headers appears in either file
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only src/audio/PipeWireCaptureStream.cpp -I src $(pkg-config --cflags libpipewire-0.3) passes or cmake --build build compiles the unit
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified

PipeWireCaptureStream exposes a bounded CaptureVisualizationSnapshot reader/publisher interface; its callback publishes only preallocated snapshot storage and never emits Qt signals or drains AudioRingBuffer
